sections.title: 2. Integrated Lab: The Broken Application Server

content.text: A single scenario touching seven of the twelve RH134 chapters. Work top to bottom — later steps assume earlier ones are fixed, exactly like a real incident.

A colleague handed you a RHEL 8 VM that's supposed to run a small internal web app off a dedicated LVM-backed volume, with a nightly backup job, before leaving the company without documenting anything. Nothing works. Root's password is unknown. Bring it fully back to life.
One RHEL 8 VM, currently failing to boot normally, SELinux enforcing, firewalld running
A second unused virtual disk /dev/vdb for the app's storage
The system drops to an emergency shell on boot because of a bad /etc/fstab entry someone left behind, AND nobody knows the root password. Recover both.

Partition /dev/vdb, build an LVM stack (VG appdata, LV weblv, 400 MiB, XFS), mount it persistently at /srv/webapp, and verify the fstab entry survives a real unmount/remount test before you ever reboot again.

The app team (group webteam) needs rwx on /srv/webapp; a single auditor account (auditor1) needs read-only, without inheriting write access for anything created later. Set this up with ACLs. Separately, confirm /srv/webapp carries a context httpd can actually serve from, and fix it if not.
The app will listen on port 8090/tcp. Open it on the active firewall zone AND confirm/add the correct SELinux port label — permanently, so it survives a reboot.

Add a system-wide cron job (the right way, not by hand-editing /etc/crontab) that runs a backup script at 01:15 every night as the webteam user. Separately, a batch log-processing script keeps starving interactive SSH sessions of CPU — fix its priority without killing it.

Write out your own command sequence for all five tasks before reading further. This lab is intentionally built to be harder without hints than any single Part's lab — that's the point of a comprehensive review.
# Reboot, interrupt GRUB, append rd.break, Ctrl+x
# System reboots, relabels, drops to emergency shell again for the bad fstab line
switch_root:/# vim /etc/fstab # remove/fix the bad entry
[root@host ~]# umount /srv/webapp && mount /srv/webapp # prove it before trusting it
auditor1's entry deliberately has no d: prefix — the requirement was read-only on the directory itself, not inherited by future files.
[root@host ~]# semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8090 # if not already listed
A clean reboot logs in normally as root with the new password — no emergency shell.
df -h /srv/webapp shows the LVM volume mounted; getfacl confirms webteam rwx (default+regular) and auditor1 r-x (regular only).
curl http://localhost:8090 (once the app is actually running) succeeds — proving BOTH firewall and SELinux port label are correct.
cat /var/log/cron or journalctl -u crond around 01:15 shows the backup job firing; ps -o nice on the log processor shows 15, not the default 0.
Mark each skill honestly. 'Can perform' means from memory, under time pressure, without opening this guide.
Write a Bash script with a for loop and an if/test condition
Search text with grep + regex (anchors, classes, -v, -r)
Schedule a one-time job with at, and a recurring one with cron.d
Enable a systemd timer as a cron alternative
Set an ACL, a default ACL, and correctly read the mask's effect
Change SELinux mode, fix a file context, toggle a boolean, read an AVC denial
Partition a disk, format it, and mount it persistently via fstab
Build a PV→VG→LV stack and extend it live (both XFS and ext4 growth commands)
Configure an autofs indirect or wildcard map
Reset the root password via rd.break
Recover from a bad fstab entry via emergency mode
Open a port in firewalld persistently, and label it correctly for SELinux
Build and validate a Kickstart file

🎯 RHCSA EXAM CRITICAL If more than two or three of these are still 'not confident,' revisit that specific Part's lab again before moving on to RH294 — RH294's automation content assumes every one of these is already second nature, because you'll be automating exactly these tasks.

sections.title: 4. Final Mixed Quiz — All RH134 Chapters

content.text: Q1. A for loop needs to iterate over host01 through host20 without typing every name. What's the cleanest way?
Answer: Brace expansion: for HOST in host{01..20}; do
Q2. A cron entry set to run on the 1st of the month AND every Monday unexpectedly fires on a Tuesday the 1st. Why?
Answer: cron's day-of-month/day-of-week fields are OR'd together when both are restricted, not AND'd — it fires when either matches.
Q3. getfacl shows user:dana:rwx #effective:r-- on a file. What's capping it, and how would you check?
Answer: The ACL mask — check with getfacl again, specifically the mask:: line.
Q4. A file moved (not copied) into /var/www/html returns 403 from Apache despite correct rwx permissions. First diagnostic command?
Answer: ls -Z — to check whether its SELinux context still reflects its OLD location (mv preserves context; cp would have inherited the new directory's).
Q5. You need to grow an ext4 filesystem after lvextend. Which command, and what argument does it take?
Answer: resize2fs, taking the LOGICAL VOLUME DEVICE (not the mount point — that's the XFS command's argument).
Q6. What fstab mount option is mandatory for a Stratis filesystem, and what breaks without it?
Answer: x-systemd.requires=stratisd.service — without it, the system can boot to emergency mode because systemd tries to mount before stratisd is running.
Q7. From an rd.break shell, what command fixes /etc/shadow's missing SELinux label after resetting the root password?
Answer: touch /.autorelabel, which forces a full relabel on the next boot.
Q8. A firewall-cmd --add-port command worked immediately in testing but the rule was gone after a reboot. What was missed?
Answer: --permanent — without it, the change is runtime-only and doesn't survive a reload or reboot.
Q9. In a Kickstart file, what three commands build an LVM layout, in order?
Answer: part pv.01 (create the PV placeholder), volgroup (build the VG from it), logvol (carve out each LV).
Q10. A service is denied even with correct file permissions, correct SELinux file context, and an open firewall port. What's the remaining layer to check?
Answer: SELinux port labeling (semanage port -l) — the process's domain may not be allowed to bind that specific port label.
RH134 is complete. Every RH294 chapter from here on assumes everything in Section 8.3's checklist is solid — RH294 doesn't re-teach storage, SELinux, or firewalld; it automates them.
RH294 will teach you to do instead
Manually running setfacl, semanage, firewall-cmd on one box
Writing an Ansible playbook that applies the same config to any number of hosts, idempotently
Writing a Kickstart file for one repeatable install
Writing a playbook + inventory that provisions and configures fleets of hosts
Bash scripts with loops and conditionals for one-off admin tasks
Ansible tasks, loops, and conditionals that describe DESIRED STATE instead of a command sequence
Manually verifying a fix worked (getfacl, ls -Z, curl)
Ansible's own idempotence check: running the same playbook twice and seeing 'ok' instead of 'changed' the second time

💡 WHY THIS MATTERS Nothing you learned in RH134 becomes obsolete — RH294 just gives you a way to stop doing it by hand, one server at a time. The mental models (PV/VG/LV, SELinux contexts, firewall zones) stay exactly the same; only the interface to them changes.
RH134 is done. Next: RH294 Part 1 — Introducing Ansible + Deploying Ansible.
